specification.problem: Given a target single-qubit unitary U (reducible to axial Z-rotations R_z(\theta) by Euler decomposition) and a precision \varepsilon, synthesize a Repeat-Until-Success (RUS) circuit over the Clifford+T gate set acting on one ancilla qubit plus the target qubit, such that on ancilla measurement outcome 0 the target undergoes a unitary within distance \varepsilon of R_z(\theta), and on outcome 1 the target undergoes a known Clifford (ideally the identity) so the attempt can be repeated; the expected T-count should be low (abstract reports on average about 2.5 times below the ancilla-free bound 3\log_2(1/\varepsilon)).
specification.reconstruction_scope: Scope chosen (no experiment_scope supplied): the RUS primitive for a single axial Z-rotation. We specify (i) the generic RUS block structure and success/failure semantics, (ii) the cyclotomic-integer parametrization z\in\mathbb{Z}[\omega], y\in\mathbb{Z}[\sqrt{2}] with |z|^2+y^2=2^L that makes the success branch an exact Z-rotation and the failure branch the identity, (iii) one explicit two-qubit unitary W over \mathbb{Z}[\omega,1/\sqrt{2}] realizing these blocks (exactly Clifford+T-synthesizable), and (iv) a tiny exact instance z=2+\omega, y=\sqrt{2}-1, L=3 giving R_z(2\arg(2+\omega)) with success probability (5+2\sqrt{2})/8. Outside scope (paper contributions not reconstructible from the abstract): the probabilistically-polynomial-time classical search that finds (z,y,L) achieving precision \varepsilon with small L, the paper's specific two-qubit circuit template and its T-count, the Euler-angle assembly for general U beyond the stated background formula, and all numerical T-count evidence.

equations.label: RUS block structure and success/failure semantics
equations.description: A two-qubit unitary W on ancilla (prepared in |0>) and target. Measuring the ancilla gives outcome 0 with probability p, applying the unitary V (the desired operation) to the target; outcome 1 applies C_fail, which must be a Clifford (so it can be undone or is the identity) and the circuit is repeated. Because A is proportional to a unitary, p is independent of |psi>, and the number of rounds is geometric with mean 1/p.
equations.justification: Standard definition of Repeat-Until-Success circuits (Paetznick–Svore style); the abstract names RUS circuits with one ancilla and measurement but does not state the relation.
assumptions: Ancilla is reset to |0> before each repetition
Failure branch is corrected by a Clifford (zero T-count) or is the identity

equations.label: Approximation metric for the target rotation
equations.description: Global-phase-invariant distance used to define 'within precision epsilon'; for two Z-rotations it reduces to a function of the angle difference. The abstract requires approximation within precision epsilon but does not fix the metric.
equations.abstract_quote: approximate any given single-qubit unitary within precision $\varepsilon$
equations.justification: The abstract asserts an epsilon-approximation; this is the metric conventionally used in Clifford+T synthesis literature, but the paper's exact choice is not given in the abstract.
assumptions: Metric choice is an assumption; operator-norm distance up to phase would differ by a constant factor

equations.label: Cyclotomic parametrization of an RUS Z-rotation
equations.description: The success branch implements an exact Z-rotation by angle 2 arg z, and the failure branch (built from the real element y) is the identity. The approximation requirement becomes d(R_z(theta), R_z(2 arg z)) <= epsilon, i.e. choosing z with argument close to theta/2 (mod pi). The norm equation forces the whole W to have entries in Z[omega,1/sqrt2].
equations.abstract_quote: Our synthesis approach uses the Clifford+$T$ basis, plus one ancilla qubit and measurement.
equations.justification: Inferred: a Clifford+T RUS circuit with one ancilla acting as an exact Z-rotation on success must have blocks with entries in Z[omega,1/sqrt2]; diag(z^*,z)/sqrt(2^L) with z in Z[omega] is the natural parametrization used in prior RUS work. The restriction y real (failure = identity) is one simple choice; the paper may allow other Clifford failure branches (e.g., y in omega^k Z[sqrt2]).
assumptions: Failure branch restricted to the identity (y real)
Paper's actual parametrization may differ in detail

equations.label: Explicit two-qubit unitary realizing the RUS blocks
equations.description: The target qubit controls which single-qubit unitary (M_0 or M_1, complex conjugates of each other) acts on the ancilla. Direct computation gives the ancilla-0 block A proportional to diag(z^*,z) and the ancilla-1 block C proportional to the identity, as required by eq_rus_structure and eq_norm_equation. Unitarity of M_1 follows exactly from |z|^2+y^2=2^L and y real. W has entries in Z[omega,1/sqrt2], hence is exactly Clifford+T-synthesizable (eq_exact_synthesis).
equations.justification: A proposed concrete construction, not stated in the abstract; the paper's own circuit template may differ. It is included so the later circuit stage has a well-defined W.
assumptions: Register order: ancilla is qubit 0 (most significant), target is qubit 1; joint basis index 2a+t
The paper's two-qubit circuit may have a different (lower T-count) form

equations.label: Exact Clifford+T synthesizability
equations.latex: U\in U(2^n),\; U_{jk}\in\mathbb{Z}[\omega,1/\sqrt{2}]\;\forall j,k\;\Longleftrightarrow\; U\text{ is exactly implementable over Clifford+}T\;(\text{for }n\ge 2\text{ possibly with one extra ancilla})
equations.description: Characterization of exactly Clifford+T-implementable unitaries: single-qubit case needs no ancilla (Kliuchnikov–Maslov–Mosca); multi-qubit case may need at most one borrowed ancilla (Giles–Selinger). Guarantees W of eq_W_construction has an exact circuit.
equations.justification: Well-known exact-synthesis theorems for the Clifford+T gate set; recalled from knowledge, not from the abstract.

equations.label: Reduction of a general single-qubit unitary to axial rotations
equations.description: Any single-qubit unitary factors (up to global phase) into three Z-rotations interleaved with Hadamards; approximating each Z-rotation by an RUS circuit with error epsilon_i yields total error bounded by the sum (triangle inequality for a unitarily invariant distance). Each RUS block is run to success before the next begins.
equations.justification: Standard Euler-angle decomposition; needed to connect the Z-rotation primitive to 'any given single-qubit unitary' in the abstract.
assumptions: Error-additivity holds for the chosen metric up to constant factors

equations.label: Reported expected T-count performance (claim, not derived)
equations.description: Expected T-count of an RUS circuit is the per-round T-count divided by the success probability (no T gates needed for correction when the failure branch is a Clifford). The abstract reports numerically that this is on average 2.5 times below the ancilla-free lower bound 3 log2(1/epsilon); this is a reported empirical claim, not a derived relation.
equations.abstract_quote: an expected $T$-count on average $2.5$ times lower than the theoretical lower bound of $3\log_{2}(1/\varepsilon)$ for ancilla-free single-qubit circuit decomposition
equations.justification: The first equality is the standard geometric-repetition cost; the approximate relation restates the abstract's numerical claim.
assumptions: Correction after failure costs no T gates

equations.label: Tiny exact instance
equations.latex: z=2+\omega,\; y=\sqrt{2}-1,\; L=3:\quad |z|^2=5+2\sqrt{2},\; y^2=3-2\sqrt{2},\; |z|^2+y^2=8,\quad p=\frac{5+2\sqrt{2}}{8}\approx 0.9786,\quad V_z=R_z\!\left(2\arctan\frac{\sqrt{2}/2}{2+\sqrt{2}/2}\right)\approx R_z(0.5110)
equations.description: A minimal concrete solution of the norm equation. The RUS circuit with M_1 = (1/sqrt8)[[2+omega, 1-sqrt2],[sqrt2-1, 2+omega^{-1}]] implements exactly R_z(2 arg(2+omega)) on success (epsilon = 0 for this target angle) and the identity on failure, with about 1.022 expected rounds.
equations.justification: Chosen as the smallest useful explicit instance for the circuit stage; verified by direct algebra (|2+omega|^2 = 4+1+2*2cos(pi/4) = 5+2sqrt2, (sqrt2-1)^2 = 3-2sqrt2).
assumptions: This instance illustrates the construction; it is not an instance from the paper

registers.name: a (ancilla)
registers.role: RUS ancilla, prepared in |0>, measured in the computational basis after W; qubit 0 (most significant in joint index 2a+t)

registers.name: t (target)
registers.role: Data qubit carrying |psi> to which R_z(2 arg z) is applied on success; qubit 1

specification.initial_state: |0\rangle_a\otimes|\psi\rangle_t with |\psi\rangle arbitrary (for a test instance, e.g. |\psi\rangle=|+\rangle=(|0\rangle+|1\rangle)/\sqrt{2} so that the phase 2\arg z is observable).

steps.description: Classical: decompose the target single-qubit unitary U into Z-rotations R_z(alpha), R_z(beta), R_z(gamma) interleaved with Hadamards; allocate precision budget per rotation.

Classical (paper's core contribution, details missing): for each angle theta, find z in Z[omega], y in Z[sqrt2], L in N with |z|^2 + y^2 = 2^L and d(R_z(theta), R_z(2 arg z)) <= epsilon, preferring small L / high p. For the toy instance use z = 2+omega, y = sqrt2-1, L = 3.
Classical: form the two-qubit unitary W from (z, y, L) and exactly synthesize it over Clifford+T.
Quantum: prepare ancilla in |0>, apply W to ancilla ⊗ target, measure the ancilla in the computational basis.

Classical control: on outcome 0 the target holds V_z|psi> = R_z(2 arg z)|psi> and the block is complete; on outcome 1 the target is unchanged (C_fail = I), reset the ancilla to |0> and repeat from the previous step. Expected rounds 1/p; expected T-count T(W)/p.
Repeat the RUS block for each of the three Euler Z-rotations (with Hadamards between them) to realize a general U.

specification.measurement: Single-qubit computational-basis measurement of the ancilla after each application of W. Outcome 0 (probability p = |z|^2/2^L, independent of |psi>) signals success; outcome 1 signals failure with the target left in state C_fail|psi> = |psi> (identity failure branch). The target qubit is not measured by the algorithm (for verification only, one may measure the target in the X/Y basis to estimate the applied phase 2 arg z).
specification.classical_postprocessing: Feed-forward only: if the ancilla outcome is 1, reset the ancilla and repeat W; stop at the first 0. Track the number of rounds; the expected count is 1/p and the expected T-count is T(W)/p. No other postprocessing.
assumptions: No experiment_scope was supplied; the scope was chosen to be the RUS primitive for a single Z-rotation with the explicit toy instance z=2+omega, y=sqrt2-1, L=3.
Register ordering: ancilla first (most significant), target second; joint basis index 2a+t.
Failure branch restricted to the identity (y real in Z[sqrt2]); the paper may permit other Clifford failure branches.
The two-qubit unitary W in eq_W_construction is a proposed realization, not the paper's circuit template.
Approximation metric taken as the global-phase-invariant trace-based distance.
Correction after failure costs no T gates; ancilla can be reset between rounds.

The paper's specific two-qubit Clifford+T circuit template for RUS circuits and its T-count as a function of L.
Whether the paper targets Z-rotations only or other axial/general unitaries directly, and how precision is budgeted across Euler angles.
The precise distance metric used to define precision epsilon.
All numerical evidence (distribution of expected T-counts, the 2.5x average improvement, and the range of epsilon studied).
